Nora Patel: Quick per-diem question from an international workshop: I was in Oslo for 3 days. Day 1 was travel (overnight), Day 2 full conference, Day 3 I left midday for a personal day. How do I claim per-diem for day 3?
Maria (People Ops): If you left midday and it became a personal day, per-diem for day 3 is prorated. Policy: full per-diem for overnight business nights, 50% for partial travel days if overnight still occurred, otherwise 0%. So Day 1 (overnight travel) = full; Day 2 = full; Day 3 = 50% if you had an overnight that night, otherwise 0%.
Nora Patel: I stayed the night before travel in a hotel because of an early flight (company paid). Does that count as Day 1 overnight business?
Maria (People Ops): Yes, pre-travel hotel nights paid/approved by the company count as overnight business nights for per-diem purposes.
Hana Kim (Sales): Also check: on Day 2 the team had a client dinner and a separate internal wrap-up dinner. Alcohol was on the client bill and on my personal receipt at the wrap-up. Is alcohol reimbursable?
Sam Patel (Finance): Client entertainment: reasonable alcohol on a client meal is allowed when the client is present and expense coded to "Client Entertainment". For internal team dinners, alcohol is not reimbursable unless pre-approved or part of an executive-level event. Attach receipts and note who was present.
Nora Patel: One receipt is missing: taxi from hotel to airport on Day 3. I paid cash and lost the receipt. I have the card statement showing other taxi charges but not that one. Any workaround?
Sam Patel (Finance): Lost cash taxi receipts: Finance requires an attestation. Provide a short note with date, amount, route, and manager confirmation. If you can get an emailed itinerary from the taxi company or a digital map screenshot with time, attach that. Otherwise we may reimburse up to a per-journey cap with manager approval.
Nora Patel: Thanks. Also asked about per-diem advance: I took a small per-diem float before travel. When I submit, should I list amounts as offsets?
Maria (People Ops): Yes, in Expensely submit per-diem as a single line and add a second line "Per-diem advance applied" with negative amount equal to the float. Attach the advance approval. Finance will net to final reimbursement.
Hana Kim (Sales): Currency conversion Q: receipts are in NOK, my card charged in GBP. Which rate do we use?
Sam Patel (Finance): Use the bank/card conversion rate shown on your proof-of-payment (card statement). If you paid cash in NOK, use the OANDA mid-market rate on the transaction date and note it. Finance will accept either but the proof-of-payment conversion is preferred.
Nora Patel: Any special notes for meals covered by the conference organizer? They provided boxed lunches on Day 2.
Maria (People Ops): If organizer-provided meals are included, subtract those meals from per-diem claim. Document which meals were provided (e.g., "Day 2 lunch provided by organizer - not claimed").
expense-bot: Reminder: attach receipts as PDFs under 10MB, redact passport numbers, and use "Per-diem - International" expense type. Include manager approval for any attestation.
Nora Patel: Great — I'll collect receipts, upload the advance docs, and add the attestation for the taxi. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
